newsitem.title: INDIA: India Essar Oil quits offshore drilling.
newsitem.headline: India Essar Oil quits offshore drilling.

text.p: Indian oil drilling services firm Essar Oil Ltd said it sold its offshore oil rigs and would no longer have any interest in offshore drilling activity.
"In view of the emerging economics in the international drilling activity, Essar Oil Ltd considers it prudent not to continue as an independent two-rig operator," it said in a statement on Tuesday.
Essar Oil said it sold the two offshore rigs for approximately 1.9 billion rupees ($53 million).
The company said it will remain active in the onshore drilling, operating 12 rigs in this sector.
Essar said it bagged two new onshore drilling contracts for 1.25 billion rupees from Petroleum Development of Oman, taking the total drilling contracts executed by it in the Middle East to seven.
"Worldwide, the independent offshore drilling companies are regrouping themselves into larger operating groups through consortia arrangements to be more competitive," Essar said.
Oil analysts said Essar Oil, which is building a refinery to process nine million tonnes of crude oil a year on the western coast, was desperately looking to raise cash.
The company has also been scouting since last year for an oil major partner for its refinery, analysts said.
